title: Molecular Dynamics Simulation of the Solidification of AlCoCuFeNi High-Entropy Alloy Nanowire
summary: Molecular dynamics simulation of the solidification behavior of an AlCoCuFeNi high-entropy alloy nanowire was performed using an embedded atom model potential at cooling rates of 10^11, 10^12, and 10^13 K/s. Periodic boundary conditions were applied along the nanowire axis to model an effectively infinite nanowire. The crystallization process was characterized through the temperature dependence of the potential energy. Structural evolution was analyzed using adaptive common-neighbor analysis (CNA) and radial distribution functions (RDF). The results show that the final structure changes from amorphous to crystalline with decreasing cooling rate, demonstrating the strong influence of cooling conditions on phase formation in nanoscale high-entropy alloy systems.

title: From Instantons to AdS Boundaries: Tracing the Geometric Path from Quantum Anomalies to Massive Gravity
summary: This thesis studies how boundary data enter two gravitational observables: the Dirac index on gravitational instantons and conserved charges in three-dimensional New Massive Gravity. In Einstein gravity coupled to ModMax electrodynamics, we compute the index of charged Dirac fermions on Taub-NUT and Eguchi-Hanson instantons using the Atiyah-Patodi-Singer theorem, which includes the spectral asymmetry of the boundary Dirac operator. The Taub-NUT index agrees with the Maxwell result. For Eguchi-Hanson, the gauge-field contribution to the axial anomaly depends explicitly on the ModMax parameter when expressed in terms of the solution parameters. For asymptotically anti-de Sitter solutions of New Massive Gravity with Brown-Henneaux boundary conditions, a term linear in the extrinsic curvature reproduces the holographic stress tensor of the auxiliary-field formulation. At the degenerate point, relaxed boundary conditions admit an additional constrained Fefferman-Graham coefficient. A quadratic extrinsic counterterm cancels the residual power divergence. We derive the boundary Ward identity and show that the holographic and Noether-Wald charges agree for the solutions studied.

title: Twisting Spinning Particles with Superghost Backgrounds
summary: We construct twists of spinning particles in the classical BV formalism by giving constant backgrounds to the bosonic ghosts of local worldline supersymmetry, in analogy with Costello and Li's twist of supergravity, which gives a nonzero background to the ghost of local spacetime supersymmetry. We represent the superghosts on polynomial states and gauge selected worldline R symmetries, imposing the shifted R constraints absolutely and the unshifted ones relatively. On flat targets, the N=2 particle, its N=4 extension on a complex target and an N=8 particle with two fermion flavors give the de Rham, Dolbeault and polynomial linear BCOV complexes. The last two are the linearized field content of the open and closed B-model target-space theories. Pairings and interactions require target-space input beyond the reduced worldline differentials.

title: Magnon high-harmonic generation by nonlinearities of spin torque driven by phonon-mediated crossing of many-body energy levels of bright and dark excitons
summary: Recent intense experimental focus on CrSBr, a two-dimensional (2D) antiferromagnetic semiconductor, has revealed numerous surprises in its response to ultrafast optical drive. We demonstrate that a single microscopic mechanism accounts for two of them---high-harmonic generation of magnons and persistence of magnon oscillations over \mbox{$\sim 1$ ns} time scale that is much longer than the femtosecond laser pulse (fsLP) pump duration. This mechanism arises from an unusually complex interplay of four different fundamental quasiparticles of condensed matter physics: magnons, optically bright and dark excitons, and phonons. By viewing magnons as the system and the other three quasiparticles as a quantum many-body bath, we derive an extended Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (eLLG) equation. Its new term generated by the bath is spatially nonlocal and time-dependent, as well as strongly {\em nonlinear} when the {\em crossing of many-body energy levels} of bright and dark excitons occurs via phonon mediation. It also resembles the so-called field-like spin-transfer torque (STT) in spintronics, but STT is driven there with current pulses, so it explains the microscopic origin of the recently experimentally conjectured {\em excitonic STT}. Since dark excitons supply energy to magnons long after the fsLP is switched off, such a reservoir opens avenues for its engineering and applications in optospintronics and optomagnonics, neuromorphic computing, and quantum transduction.

title: Precise experimental investigation of the reflection properties caused by s-polarized evanescent waves and the Casimir puzzle
comment: 19 pages, 8 figures; accepted for publication in Phys. Rev. A
summary: We report a high-precision experiment on measuring the low-frequency magnetic field reflected from a metallic plate. This experiment is designed to give insight into why theoretical predictions of the fundamental Lifshitz theory using the standard response function to the electromagnetic waves are in contradiction with the data of numerous precision measurements of the Casimir force (the Casimir puzzle). To attain these ends, we measured the magnitude and phase of the lateral component of the magnetic field produced by an oscillating magnetic dipole and reflected from a metallic plate. These quantities are completely determined by the evanescent waves with the transverse electric (s) polarization. The obtained measurement data are compared with theoretical predictions using the standard Drude response function of the metal to the low-frequency electromagnetic waves. It is shown that there are both quantitative and qualitative disagreements with these predictions, so that in the region of low-frequency s-polarized evanescent waves the Drude response function is excluded by the data. Keeping in mind that just the s-polarized evanescent waves are responsible for the Casimir puzzle, our results highlight the causes for its emergence. It is emphasized that, in addition to the Casimir effect, searching for the adequate nonlocal response functions of metals to the evanescent waves is of utmost significance for many areas of physics as near-field optical microscopy, nanophotonics, surface plasmon polaritons, radiative heat transfer, and others.

title: Holographic Duals of $SL^{(q)}(2, \mathbb{R})$ Deformed CFTs
summary: We study the holographic bulk dual of 2D CFTs evolved by $sl^{(q)}(2,R)$-deformed Hamiltonians. Working in the Hamiltonian-adapted frame, in which the $sl^{(q)}(2,R)$-deformed effective Floquet Hamiltonian generates time translations, we construct the dual Bañados geometries for the three distinct classes of dynamics: the heating phase, the non-heating phase and the phase boundary. Specifically, we show that in the heating phase, the bulk patch dual to the region between two neighbouring fixed points has a time-dependent causal horizon and asymptotes to a static AdS Rindler geometry at late times, while the non-heating phase has no horizon. We discuss how the late-time behaviour of the entanglement entropy, particularly its linear growth in the heating phase, can be understood from the bulk in two different ways: in global AdS, from the portion of the geodesic behind the horizons, and in a quotient description, from an effective shockwave produced by a boosted conical defect. Finally, for ($q=1$), we complete the holographic analysis of Ref. [1] by reproducing the exact CFT expression of the OTOC from the bulk and explaining why it exhibits an exponential growth {\it only} when the operators lie on the side of the two fixed points.

title: Scalable Simulation of Strongly Correlated Fermions with Neural Gaussian Tensor Networks
summary: Accurate simulations of strongly correlated electrons remain a central challenge in computational physics. We introduce neural-network Gaussian projected entangled-pair states (NN-GPEPS), which exploit the locally-entangled subspace of Gaussian states to give an architecture more compatible with modern neural networks and an exact contraction cost of $O(N^{3/2})$ on two-dimensional lattices. For the Hubbard model at $U/t=8$ and $1/8$ hole doping, we obtain state-of-the-art variational energies in large lattices of up to 1024 sites. These results demonstrate an accurate approach to strongly correlated fermions by connecting neural networks with Gaussian tensor networks.

title: momipy: A time-resolved momentum microscopy data analysis workflow
summary: Photoemission momentum microscopy is an emerging approach to photoelectron spectroscopy that is transforming electronic band structure mapping at both laboratory-based and large-scale facilities. Its extension to time-resolved measurements has recently enabled major advances, ranging from the femtosecond imaging of exciton wavefunctions to dark-field photoelectron microscopy of light-induced dynamics and strong light-matter interactions. However, the rapid acquisition of high-dimensional data sets (including electron in-plane momenta $k_x$ and $k_y$, kinetic energy $E_\mathrm{kin}$, time $Δt$, and more) poses substantial challenges for data handling and analysis. A typical workflow encompasses data acquisition, exploratory visualization, calibration and targeted feature extraction, with data management ideally guided by FAIR principles. Here, we present momipy, a Python package that streamlines the momentum microscopy data analysis workflow efficiently and at low computational cost. Among other features, momipy provides interactive 4D data visualization, energy and momentum calibration, space-charge correction, and a broad selection of multidimensional data analysis routines, including binning, momentum-map extraction and time-, energy- and momentum-resolved model fitting. momipy is accompanied by a selection of interactive example scripts, supporting adoption of momipy by both experienced researchers and users new to momentum microscopy.

title: Upper Bounds on the Radion Mass in a Warped Extra Dimension
summary: We study absolute upper bounds on the mass ratio $R_{11}=m_{r_1}/m_{h_1}$ between the radion ($r_1$) and graviton ($h_1$) lightest modes in five dimensional warped models. We consider warped models with an admissible singular behavior in the infrared: i.e.~models with power-like ($\sim \barφ^{2n}$) and with exponential ($\sim e^{2ν\barφ}$) bulk potentials, where $\barφ$ is the stabilizing bulk field. We find a correlation between $R_{11}$ and the singular behavior of the Ricci scalar, which allows to establish an absolute upper bound on the former. For the power-like models, the maximum value of $R_{11}$ increases with $n$. In the limit $n\to\infty$, the power-like model reproduces the exponential model and reaches the same upper bound as the latter. For the exponential model, we derive analytically the bound $R_{11}<1$, with the largest value approached for the case $ν\to 1^+$ (where $ν=1$ corresponds to the linear dilaton model) and consistent with unitarity sum rules. For exponential models we also obtain the absolute upper bound on the second radion mode ratio $R_{21}=m_{r_2}/m_{h_1}\lesssim 1.374$. This value is reached for $ν=2$ when the IR brane approaches the singularity. For this configuration, we verify that the scalar contribution satisfies the unitarity sum rule when the complete radion Kaluza-Klein tower is included.

title: $C_T$ and $C_J$ of general scalar--fermion conformal field theories in $d=4-ε$
summary: We compute $C_T$ and $C_J$, the coefficients of the stress-tensor and conserved-current two-point functions, to order $ε^3$ at any fixed point of the general renormalizable theory of scalars and fermions in $d=4-ε$. We give explicit results for the chiral Ising, XY and Heisenberg models and for fixed points with emergent supersymmetry in $d=3$. In theories without a four-dimensional counterpart, fermion loops with an odd number of Yukawa vertices contribute at order $ε^3$ through traces whose continuation away from $d=3$ is ambiguous; we fix it with $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetry, by computing the two-point functions of the supercurrent and of the fermionic partner of a flavor current to four loops. In $d=3$, Padé approximants closely reproduce the exact $C_T$ of the $\mathcal N=2$ super-Ising model. We estimate the universal conductivity at the charge-density-wave, Kekulé and Néel transitions of graphene to be $σ/σ_{\rm free}\approx0.91$, $0.79$--$0.83$ and $0.64$--$0.74$, and show that the exact conductivity at the supersymmetric transition on the surface of a topological insulator is $σ/σ_{\rm free}=\frac{9}{10}\,C_T/C_{T,\rm free}\approx0.654$, $10\%$ below the value previously reported.

title: Ab-initio study of magnetic interaction in RNiO2: role of rare-earth size and epitaxial strain
summary: In this paper we present a systematic first-principles investigation of the structure and nearest-neighbor magnetic exchange interactions in the infinite-layer RNiO2 thin-film series (R = La-Lu), under the constrain of different substrates. Density functional theory calculations are first employed to optimize the crystal structures, while CAS+DDCI correlated wave-function calculations were used for the determination of the magnetic exchanges. This methodology allows to obtain magnetic interactions in good agreement with RIXS experimental estimations. In the pristine case, our results confirm that the structure of RNiO2 (except for R = La and Ce) adopts the I4/mcm space group, characterized by an out-of-plane rotation of the NiO4 plaquettes. This result remains valid under substrate constrains, even if compressive strain reduces the amplitude of the rotational distortion and leads to an enhancement of the magnetic exchange interaction relative to the pristine structures. The latter are found to depend sensitively on both the rare-earth ionic radius and the applied epitaxial strain. These results highlight the role of structural distortions and substrate-induced strain in tuning magnetic interactions in infinite-layer nickelates.

title: Pairwise fermionic mode correlations in electric and magnetic backgrounds: Landau-level structure and Schwinger production
summary: We investigate mutual information and logarithmic negativity in fermionic Schwinger pair production in parallel electric and magnetic fields. Using spin-dependent Bogoliubov transformations, we construct the in-vacuum and derive the particle--antiparticle correlations for selected Landau modes. We also consider an initially entangled two-particle state and evaluate the correlations for six bipartitions. The physical Landau-level structure is treated explicitly by distinguishing modes with the same oscillator index from the spin representatives of a common physical Landau level. For matched higher levels, the pairwise redistribution relations retain the electric-only form, with the magnetic-field dependence entering through the Landau-level pair-production probabilities. When the two particle groups occupy different physical levels, the cross particle--antiparticle correlations become unequal, and we derive analytic relations characterizing this asymmetry. We further obtain the local logarithmic negativity from the ordinary partial transpose in a fixed occupation-space basis. Finally, we extend the analysis to a Sauter-type electric field in a constant magnetic background and examine the dependence of the pairwise correlations on the field parameters and Landau-level structure.

title: Field theory and the biquadratic spin-1 chain
summary: The antiferromagnetic biquadratic spin-1 chain is gapped, $SU(3)$ symmetric, and integrable. Standard arguments suggest that its low-energy physics is described by the $\mathbb{CP}^2$ nonlinear sigma model at $θ=π$. Using the Bethe ansatz, we show that its low-energy excitations can be interpreted as deconfined domain walls, just as in the sigma model. However, the lattice model is integrable, whereas the field theory is generally believed not to be. We propose a solution to this mystery by finding an integrable field theory with the same low-energy limit but which is not Lorentz invariant. The integrability-preserving scaling limit is obtained by adding a higher conserved charge and tuning the chain to criticality. The gap closes quadratically, so that the limit must be described by some nonrelativistic field theory rather than the relativistic sigma model. We describe the two-particle scattering matrix of this field theory.

title: Large transformation strain of $\mathrm{Ni}_{50}\mathrm{Fe}_{23}\mathrm{Ga}_{27}$ microwires produced by the Taylor-Ulitovsky method
summary: The martensitic transformation and associated tensile strain of $\mathrm{Ni}_{50}\mathrm{Fe}_{23}\mathrm{Ga}_{27}$ microwires produced by the Taylor--Ulitovsky method were investigated using thermomechanical analysis, electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD), and in-situ tensile X-ray diffraction (XRD). EBSD mapping at room temperature reveals cubic austenite in a nonstrained part of the microwire and tetragonal martensite in the strained part. Both EBSD and XRD show that both austenite and martensite have $[001]$ directions approximately parallel to the wire axis. The axial transformation strain calculated from the measured lattice parameters is approximately $15.4\%$. Thermal cycling under constant stresses of $20\text{--}100~\mathrm{MPa}$ reveals experimental transformation strains of $13.2\text{--}14.0\%$. Increasing tensile stress raises the transformation temperatures, with a stress--temperature slope of approximately $1.52~\mathrm{MPa}/^\circ\mathrm{C}$, comparable to that reported for $[001]$-oriented $\mathrm{Ni\text{--}Fe\text{--}Ga}$ single crystals. Overall, the observations confirm that the large macroscopic strain of up to $14.0\%$ relates to the nearly complete martensitic transformation in the microwire.

title: From Integrability to Chaos in Tensionless AdS3 String Theory
comment: This paper is an expanded version of Section 5 of arXiv:2605.06465v1. Correspondingly, Section 5 of arXiv:2605.06465v2 has been shortened
summary: We study quantum-gravitational corrections to the planar integrable structure of the symmetric product orbifold $\text{Sym}^N(\mathbb{T}^4)$ that is dual to tensionless string theory on AdS$_3\times$S$^3\times \mathbb{T}^4$. We consider the deformation that switches on R-R flux in the bulk, and analyze the associated level spacing statistics. The leading non-planar corrections lift the planar degeneracies and produce signs of random-matrix behavior. Our results provide a controlled example of string interactions driving the onset of quantum chaos.

title: Thermal investigation of buffer and transition layers in AlGaN HEMT stacks
summary: In this work, we investigate thermal transport in a set of thin-film layers used in modern HEMT designs. Our theoretical analysis employs three phonon-transport models of increasing sophistication, ranging from a relatively simple Debye-approximation model to a first-principles framework that incorporates Density Functional Theory (DFT)-derived harmonic and anharmonic phonon properties. To describe ternary semiconductors, alloy scattering is also considered, and to account for the properties of non-ideal, polycrystalline thin films, scattering at grain and film boundaries is taken into account. For modeling the specific samples at hand, the latter are fitted to thermal conductivity data measured with Time-Domain Thermoreflectance (TDTR). Overall, we find that the first-principles model performs best and produces the most physically consistent results. Special emphasis is placed on establishing a reliable procedure for determining intrinsic transport properties dominated by Umklapp scattering. Building on these, it is then possible to systematically add additional scattering terms to the models and assess how model-inherent factors, such as the treatment of scattering rates or the description of the phonon dispersion, affect model accuracy and overall predictive capabilities.

title: A full-color four-point form factor
summary: We determine the symbol and complete functions of the full-color two-loop four-point maximally helicity violating stress-tensor form factor in $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang-Mills theory, including $N^1$ double traces and $N^0$ single traces. Numerical unitarity and a master-integral bootstrap fix the result. A direct form-factor bootstrap reproduces the symbol. Permuting external legs in the planar 88-letter alphabet yields all 79 letters, while the $N^0$ terms contain four new nonclassical contributions. We also obtain the complete $N^0$ two-loop triple-collinear hard splitting functions.

title: Alloying effects on the interface cohesion of grain boundaries in the Ni--Fe--Cr system
summary: Grain boundaries (GBs) in polycrystalline Ni-based alloys strongly influence mechanical strength and fracture behavior, yet the effect of alloying elements such as Fe and Cr on GB cohesion remains difficult to quantify systematically. Using density functional theory (DFT), we compute rigid-body separation (RBS) curves for six symmetric-tilt Ni GBs, extracting the work of separation $W_{\mathrm{sep}}$ and maximum traction $σ_{\max}$ via the universal binding energy relation (UBER). We find that substitution of Cr or Fe into the GB plane increases both quantities relative to pure Ni GBs. To overcome the size limitations of DFT, we compare several machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP) foundation models against the DFT dataset and identify a model achieving quantitative agreement with DFT for $W_{\mathrm{sep}}$ and $σ_{\max}$. This MLIP enables systematic sampling of alloying configurations at finer concentration steps. We show that alloying-induced changes in GB cohesion depend on both, element type and local structures, revealing trends that are inaccessible with DFT alone. Extending the analysis to a ternary $\mathrm{Ni}_{56}\mathrm{Fe}_{20}\mathrm{Cr}_{24}$ composition, inspired by the principal constituents of the widely used commercial Alloy 718, shows that the binary trends provide a useful basis for interpreting the combined effect of both substitutes, while explicit ternary calculations are required to capture their interplay quantitatively. Together, these results provide a validated workflow for quantifying the effect of alloying elements on GB cohesion in multicomponent alloys. The resulting values may serve as input for continuum-scale fracture models, paving the way toward atomistically informed multiscale modeling.

title: Two Faces of Spacetime Density Matrices: Entanglement and Complexity
summary: We establish a direct connection between entanglement and complexity through spacetime density matrices. For stationary pure states and complementary regions at different times, spacetime replica moments encode the return amplitude of a replica-defect quench. This representation defines an associated state spread complexity, which we call Krylov-Rényi complexity. It can equivalently be obtained by using a replica-defect excitation of the replicated background state as the seed and evolving it under the original replicated Hamiltonian. We further construct Krylov-von Neumann complexity as a probe limit from first-order replica data. Timelike entanglement and complexity provide complementary information at a fixed time, while the full time dependence of the timelike entropy determines the Krylov dynamics and hence the complexity. The replica construction fixes the seed and its evolution through the background state, subsystem geometry, and regulator, without an independently chosen probe operator. Like entanglement entropy, the resulting complexity is defined nonperturbatively and probes universal properties and dynamical information about the underlying theory.

title: Multicharged Kramers-Weyl Fermions, Quantum Geometric Hall Responses and de Haas-van Alphen Oscillations in WAl$_2$
summary: Quantum geometry of Bloch wave functions and crystalline symmetries play a central role in condensed matter physics, shaping the electronic topology and physical responses of solids. In particular, Kramers-Weyl fermions, spin-split Fermi surfaces probed through quantum oscillations and quantum geometric nonlinear Hall and intrinsic spin Hall responses have garnered significant attention. Despite progress in understanding these phenomena individually, their coexistence with topological surface states, Fermi arcs and chirality dependent quantum geometric transport remains scarce, as pronounced responses involve suitable symmetries, SOC and Fermi surface geometry. Here, we explore this synergy in experimentally synthesized WAl$_2$, considering both structural enantiomers using first-principles calculations and symmetry analysis. We observed twelve Kramers-Weyl (KW) crossings with quantized chiral charges $|C|=1$ and $|C|=3$, accompanied by nontrivial surface states and Fermi arcs. The pronounced metallic character gives rise to six Fermi surface sheets exhibiting antisymmetric SOC, with distinct extremal orbits and candidate spin-split pairs resolved through calculated de Haas-van Alphen (dHvA) quantum oscillations. The electronic structure also exhibits large intrinsic Berry curvature dipole (BCD) arising from the asymmetric distribution of Berry curvature, giving rise to a nonlinear Hall response. The opposite structural handedness of the two enantiomers reverses the chiralities and BCD, reversing the direction of Fermi arcs and nonlinear Hall current. BCD attains $|D_{zz}|\approx0.338$, yielding nonlinear Hall current densities $|j_x|\approx5.04\times10^{10}~\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$ and $|j_y|\approx2.52\times10^{10}~\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$. We observe enhanced SHC associated with triply charged KW point at $Γ$, suggesting role of higher Chern number in the SHC.

title: Second-order formulation of chiral fermions with a local boundary condition
summary: Chiral fermions in $d$ dimensions arise naturally as boundary modes of a massive fermion in $d+1$ dimensions subject to a local boundary condition. When anomalies are absent, this construction can be used to define an intrinsically $d$-dimensional theory of chiral fermions. However, defining the path integral using the first-order Dirac operator with this boundary condition is technically inconvenient, even in the continuum. We present a formulation in terms of second-order differential operators that is completely equivalent to the original formulation in the continuum. Its natural lattice discretization generates Wilson's term and avoids fermion doubling. Our lattice formulation closely resembles the boundary-fermion construction of Shamir, and provides some insight into the case of a general Wilson parameter.

title: Lattice dynamics study of (Bi1-xSbx)2Te3 compounds: Comparative compositional study of force constants and Grüneisen parameters
summary: We performed a comprehensive Raman spectroscopy study of (Bi1-xSbx)2Te3 (BST-x) compounds, with varying Sb concentration, under ambient and high-pressure conditions. At ambient conditions, the frequency of all observed Raman-active modes (E1g, A11g, E2g, A21g) is blue-shifting with increasing Sb concentration, albeit with varying concentration-dependent rate. Based on these results, we calculated the relative force constants as a function of Sb concentration using a harmonic approximation, which shows a mode-dependent variation. The force constants for the lower frequency Raman modes (E1 g and A11g) remain almost composition-independent, while for the higher-frequency ones a profound softening (E2g) or stiffening (A21g) was determined. From the Raman spectroscopy measurements under high-pressure conditions, the corresponding Grüneisen parameters for the three observed Raman-active modes (A11g, E2g, A21g) as a function of composition were determined by combining them with the previously reported Equation of States and the corresponding bulk modulus B0 of the ambient-conditions R-3m phase. The average Grüneisen parameter exhibits a clear maximum for BST-07. Based on Slack's equation, these results are directly related to the optimal ZT values for this composition. Our study provides a solid framework for connecting composition, lattice dynamics, and thermal-transport behaviour, towards establishing the microscopic origin of thermoelectric optimization in BST compounds.

title: Holographic Tessellations Tensor Networks $\{p,q\}$ from Entangled Quantum Tetrahedron in Loop Quantum Gravity
summary: The relationship between spin network states in loop quantum gravity and bulk--boundary duality is further explored using the tessellated holographic tensor network. We develop a holographic tensor network construction based on quantum entanglement between tetrahedra in loop quantum gravity (LQG). This construction relates four-valent intertwiner spaces and Bell states dressed with $SU(2)$ holonomies to effective tensors on hyperbolic $\{p,q\}$ tessellations. For the $\{5,4\}$ tessellation, six tetrahedra are assembled into a single effective cell with five network legs and one logical index. Provided that the microscopic transfer map has full row rank, a right inverse and a completion on the kernel space are employed to construct an isometric embedding, yielding an effective tensor proportional to a perfect tensor. The construction is generalized to the $p=2n-1$ family, with local dimensions supporting absolutely maximally entangled states. On finite networks satisfying a radial orientation condition, an appropriate normalization produces an isometric bulk--boundary map. For cuts satisfying the isometry condition on both sides, the boundary entropy decomposes into a link contribution $\sum_{\ell}\log(2j_{\ell}+1)$ and the bulk entropy, thereby providing a discrete realization of the quantum Ryu--Takayanagi structure. Applications to the black hole interior are formulated via postselection-based non-isometric encoding. Assuming additional Haar statistics, this framework is used to analyze the preservation of overlaps on average and the competition between entropy branches underlying the Page Curve. These results establish a constructive link between the geometric degrees of freedom of LQG and holographic codes, while clarifying the conditions required to connect them to geometric area in LQG, the location of the quantum extremal surface, and evaporation of black hole.

title: Reward misalignment as an opportunity for materials discovery
comment: 33 pages (15 pages main text and 18 pages Supplementary Information), 4 figures
summary: Reward misalignment is usually regarded as a failure of artificial intelligence. In materials discovery with generative AI models, however, disagreement between predefined rewards and expert judgment may reveal materials that the rewards overlook. We investigate this possibility using electronic flat bands as a prime example. Experts mostly agree with a numerical bandwidth score, but their disagreements are systematic and cannot be explained by an estimated 5% rate of mistaken labels. We learn the experts' preferences from pairwise comparisons and use them to guide a crystal diffusion model. The learned preferences and numerical score agree on the flattest bands but diverge elsewhere. For example, the preferences favor KCo2As2 and CoGa, reported compounds with partially flat bands that the score would discard. The framework also extends to synthesizability and phonon properties. Our findings suggest that reward misalignment can expose opportunities for materials discovery beyond what fixed rewards are designed to find.

title: Worldsheet Effective Theory of Abelian-Higgs Cosmic Strings beyond Nambu--Goto
comment: 26 pages (13 for main text, 13 for appendices). 8 figures (6 in main text). Movies of the simulations can be found in https://youtu.be/tlT1DMFg6DY and https://youtu.be/O7oJLk80Ce4 . Comments are welcome
summary: Cosmic strings can support long-lived excitations confined to their cores, opening channels for energy exchange with the transverse Goldstone modes that describe the string's motion. We derive a covariant worldsheet theory of their coupled dynamics directly from the Abelian-Higgs model at critical coupling, with all interaction coefficients fixed by the microscopic theory. The resulting action, which we validate against numerical lattice field theory simulations, extends the Nambu--Goto description to include a massive scalar shape mode and a massive vector mode. Dualizing the vector reveals a geometric distinction: the shape scalar mode couples to intrinsic worldsheet curvature, while the pseudoscalar couples to normal bundle curvature. These interactions explain the distinct parametric instabilities observed in lattice simulations and predict how the relative polarization of colliding transverse waves controls the excitation of the two internal modes. Our results connect microscopic string structure to the nonlinear worldsheet dynamics, providing a predictive framework for cosmic strings beyond the Nambu--Goto approximation.

title: Unusual increase in electrical and thermal conductivity of severely deformed CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy: Roles of disordering and nanostructuring in electron and phonon transport
summary: This work investigates how defect engineering and nanostructuring via severe plastic deformation influence electrical and thermal transport in the high-entropy alloy CrMnFeCoNi. High-pressure torsion (HPT) for up to N = 4 turns produces a hierarchical defect structure, including deformation twins at low strains, dislocations and Lomer-Cottrell locks at intermediate strains, and a high fraction of high-angle grain boundaries at large strains. While hardness naturally increases and saturates at ~520 Hv, both electrical and thermal conductivity exhibit an unusual increase upon HPT processing (from 0.953 MS m-1 and 10.3 W m-1 K-1 after homogenization to 1.003 +- 0.005 MS m-1 and 14.4 W m-1 K-1 after N = 4). Analysis based on the Wiedemann-Franz law indicates a modest increase in electron transport (~5%) and a significant increase in phonon transport (~100%) after HPT processing. The phonon mean free path remains small on the order of 0.6-1.1 nm, and comparison with the Cahill-Pohl model shows that heat transport occurs near the minimum thermal conductivity limit, where vibrational modes are strongly scattered. This suggests that the enhancement in thermal transport is not governed by conventional defect scattering, but it is hypothesized that modifications in atomic-scale disorder, such as deformation-induced short-range ordering, are responsible for this unusual behavior. Specific heat capacity increases after HPT, consistent with stored defect energy. The linear thermal expansion exhibits a non-monotonic behavior, decreasing initially due to internal stresses and relaxation effects, and increasing at higher strains due to grain boundary-induced anharmonicity. These findings highlight the complex interplay between defects, atomic-scale disorder, and nanostructure in governing the electrical and thermal properties of severely deformed high-entropy alloys via electron and phonon scattering.

title: Equilibrium relativistic spin magnetohydrodynamics from chiral kinetic theory
summary: We develop a microscopic and thermodynamically consistent framework for relativistic equilibrium spin magnetohydrodynamics of massless chiral fermions, directly from first-order chiral kinetic theory. Starting from the covariant Wigner function, we recast the chiral kinetic equation as a pure streaming equation on a magnetically shifted mass shell, incorporating both the magnetic-moment energy and the Berry-curvature phase-space measure. This formulation yields a kinetic $H$-theorem and an entropy current with vanishing divergence in global equilibrium. We construct the equilibrium distribution for an arbitrary spin frame and derive the associated currents, energy--momentum tensor, spin tensor, entropy current, and frame-independent spin polarization, including the magnetic splitting between particles and antiparticles. Thermodynamic consistency further determines the second-order magnetovortical responses, revealing a relativistic Barnett magnetization, a temperature- and chemical-potential-independent anomalous charge density, and rotation-induced density corrections that reproduce exact field-theory results. Our framework provides a unified microscopic foundation for relativistic equilibrium spin magnetohydrodynamics and establishes a direct link between quantum kinetic theory, spin polarization, magnetization, and anomalous transport.

title: Perfumer: A Large Language Model-based Agentic Framework Accelerating Structural Relaxation and Electronic Band Prediction for First-Principle Calculation
summary: First-principles structural relaxation and band calculations require substantial computation and expertise. Here we present Perfumer, a large language model-based agentic framework that couples Quantum ESPRESSO with two predictive models. Across tested structures, pre-relaxation with Perfumer-relax model followed by QE refinement yielded a 2.75-fold overall speedup over QE alone. Perfumer-band model combines a periodic graph neural network with a latent Hermitian spectral head returns 12 band energies at any requested wavevector, preserving reciprocal lattice periodicity and time-reversal symmetry without constructing Hamiltonian. Trained on 125,153 self-curated band structures, Perfumer-band model reaches a median per-material mean absolute error of 0.157 eV on 2,607 test materials, including lanthanide, actinide and magnetic compounds, from held-out composition families spanning 85 elements, taking about 97 ms per material on two consumer CPU cores. The agent turns natural-language requests into relaxation-to-band workflows, from a single uploaded structure to automatically constructed new candidates and returns predicted properties.

title: Cardinal RG=GR: Phase-Space Cardinality and the Cosmological Constant and Hierarchy Problems
summary: The effective field theory approach constructs the low-energy theory by integrating out fluctuations above an ultraviolet scale which raises the cosmological constant and hierarchy problems. We investigate an alternative prescription in which the quantum theory is restricted to a finite accessible region of phase space, characterized by a dimensionless cardinality $\mathcal N$, rather than by independently prescribed spacetime and momentum scales. At fixed cardinality these scales are related. For Euclidean de Sitter space, the stationarity condition for the gravitational action can then be written as a stationarity condition with respect to the momentum scale, a relation which we call Cardinal RG=GR. We demonstrate the relation between $\mathcal N$ and the Gibbons-Hawking entropy of de Sitter space, compute the cosmological constant proportional to ${1}/{\sqrt{\mathcal N}}$, show that it is radiatively stable and apply the same prescription to demonstrate the radiative stability of the mass parameter for a simple interacting scalar field model, thereby illuminating the resolution of the hierarchy problem. We also establish a precise limit, involving gravitational data, in which the conventional results of Quantum Field Theory and the Renormalization Group are recovered.

title: Two distinct notions of speed in antiferromagnets
summary: The terahertz resonance frequencies of antiferromagnets characterize their precessional dynamics but do not necessarily imply faster laser-induced quenching of magnetic order. Here, we investigate the distinct roles of magnetic compensation and electronic scattering phase space by comparing ultrafast demagnetization in the antiferromagnetic charge-transfer insulator NiO, the metallic antiferromagnet Mn2Au, and a ferromagnetic Ni reference. The extracted response in Mn2Au is approximately four times faster than in NiO and substantially faster than in Ni. These observations are consistent with exchange-mediated scattering between antiparallel sublattices enabling rapid loss of antiferromagnetic order without requiring net angular-momentum transfer to an external reservoir, provided sufficient electronic scattering phase space is available. In insulating NiO, restricted electronic scattering channels reduces the ultrafast response. Our results distinguish ultrafast demagnetization from exchange-enhanced precession and identify the interplay of spin-flip probability and electronic scattering rate as a key factor governing the nonequilibrium response of compensated magnets.

title: Full-Color Two-loop Four-point Form Factor in N=4 SYM with Global CK-duality
summary: We determine the full-color two-loop four-point MHV form factor of the stress-tensor supermultiplet in N=4 super-Yang-Mills theory. Using color-kinematics (CK) duality and unitarity cuts, we construct complete one- and two-loop integrands manifesting global off-shell CK duality without explicit $μ^2$ dependence. Integration-by-parts reduction to uniform-transcendentality master integrals yields purely rational numbers multiplying simple kinematic prefactors, manifesting maximal transcendentality. Expressing the form factor in terms of pentagon functions, we verify full-color infrared-pole cancellation, extract the finite remainder, and obtain new non-planar results for the two-loop triple-collinear splitting function and double-soft current.

title: Constitutive Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks in Finite Element Model Updating: Closed-Form Hyperelastic Strain Energies from Heterogeneous Experiments
summary: Calibrating a hyperelastic constitutive model for a soft material traditionally poses two problems: an expert must choose its functional form, and several homogeneous tests must determine its parameters. Neural constitutive models solve the first, but either remain black boxes or draw on a library of candidate terms fixed in advance. Full-field measurements, such as those from digital image correlation (DIC), promise to solve the second, replacing those tests by a single heterogeneous one. Two gaps remain: flexibility during training with interpretability afterwards, and a way to train such a model on one heterogeneous test. Here we close both. We embed a constitutive Kolmogorov-Arnold network (CKAN) in finite element model updating (FEMU) and train it by minimizing the mismatch between the predicted and the measured kinematic fields and reaction forces. Pruning and symbolic regression then reduce the trained network to a compact closed-form strain energy that satisfies every constitutive requirement. On perforated natural-rubber membranes, the CKANs reproduce the DIC displacement fields with median errors between one and two percent, and transfer to a hole pattern withheld from training. On a perforated silicone plate, a CKAN trained on one stretch profile at a single load reproduces that profile and the measured reaction force to within a few percent. On an aortic specimen inflated under pressure, an anisotropic CKAN predicts the inflated three-dimensional shape. The discovered closed-form energies match the CKANs they replace on the training data and can be compared directly with established models.

title: Exact Spherical Branes and Deformations: BMN, IKKT and $\mathcal{N}=2^\ast$
summary: We present a unified analytic solution to the BPS equations of spherical Dp-branes for $1\leq p \leq 5$ and give the corresponding type II uplifts in closed form. These are holographically dual to maximally supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory on $S^{p+1}$. The change of variables that makes the BPS equations integrable also allows us to analytically calculate a universal result for the holographic Wilson loop and obtain UV asymptotic behaviour previously determined numerically. The same change of variables extends naturally, with suitable modifications, to the cases $p=0$ and $p=-1$. We obtain a 1-parameter family of D0-brane solutions and show how the IR conditions lead to a singular limit of the integration constant. We also solve the D(-1)-brane BPS equations and show the resulting Euclidean uplift fails regularity conditions. Separately, we obtain an explicit representation of the one-ball electrostatic solution of polarised IKKT, which lets us express multipole moments and holographic observables using elliptic invariants. Finally, we analytically solve the BPS equations of the holographic dual of $\mathcal{N}=2^\ast$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory on $S^4$, present the corresponding type IIB uplift and calculate the holographic Wilson loop.

title: Emergent Fatigue Dynamics from Foundational Interatomic Potentials
summary: Foundational machine-learned interatomic potentials are trained on large, diverse DFT datasets, but their validation rests on equilibrium states, which does not guarantee correct emergent behavior in large-scale molecular dynamics. Where no direct experimental validation is available, comparisons to physically motivated potentials are valuable for drawing insight. We distinguish static properties, which are thermally accessible, from emergent properties, which require work from an external fatigue stress to drive rare events, and compare the potentials on both. An EAM potential and the NequIP foundational potential both agree closely with reference data for many near-equilibrium properties, but NequIP predicts an anomalously low intrinsic stacking fault energy ($\sim7$ times lower than EAM) and thus predicts far more plastic deformation under fatigue cycling of a nanoscale flaw modeled after the classical Griffith crack problem. Per-atom energy distributions after loading show that the two potentials differ most at energies far above what is thermally accessible. We also document memory-related crashes and silent extrapolation as practical concerns for practitioners of these foundational model forms.

title: All-Order Linearized Hydrodynamics of Charged Holographic Plasmas
summary: We investigate linearized all-order transport in a finite-density holographic plasma described by five-dimensional Einstein-Maxwell-Chern-Simons theory. By retaining the full frequency- and momentum-dependence of the fluid/gravity equations, we determine generalized shear, diffusion, higher-gradient, and chiral-vortical transport functions together with their real-time memory kernels. The different channels exhibit a clear hierarchy of temporal response: the leading shear and diffusion sectors respond promptly, whereas the higher-gradient sectors develop only after a finite buildup time. Remarkably, the chiral-vortical response also shows a finite buildup time despite entering at first order in the hydrodynamic derivative expansion, demonstrating that derivative order does not by itself determine the temporal organization of transport. Toward the near-extremal regime, long-time memory becomes increasingly persistent across several channels. These results reveal how finite density reshapes nonlocal transport and relaxation in strongly coupled holographic plasmas.

title: Comparative First-Principles Study of the Physical Properties, Phonon-Mediated Superconductivity and Functional Potential of Technetium-Based Binary Borides TcB2, Tc2B and Tc3B
summary: Phonon-mediated superconductivity in binary transition-metal borides reflects a balance between the metal d-states, metal-boron bonding, and the lattice vibrations that couple to them. Here, we compare P6/mmm TcB2 at 20 GPa with I4/mcm Tc2B and P4/mmm Tc3B at 0 GPa within a first-principles framework. Their mechanical responses differ appreciably: TcB2 is the most rigid under its compressed condition, Tc2B shows the strongest tendency toward ductility, and Tc3B falls between the two. Despite these differences, all three phases remain metallic. The states at the Fermi level are dominated by Tc-4d character, although the extent of Tc-d/B-p mixing varies from one compound to another. Charge redistribution is more directional and B-centered in TcB2, but more delocalized around the Tc network in Tc2B and Tc3B. Inclusion of spin-orbit coupling leaves all three compounds metallic. The optical response remains metallic and electric field polarization dependent, with substantial visible reflectivity and strong ultraviolet absorption. Low-frequency Tc rich vibrations dominate the electron-phonon coupling (EPC). With μ* = 0.10, the Tc values of TcB2, Tc2B, and Tc3B are 24.92, 11.07, and 15.12 K, respectively. Although Tc3B exhibits a higher electronic density of states at the Fermi level, N(EF), TcB2 couples most strongly to EPC-active low-frequency modes, showing that the superconducting hierarchy depends on electronic-phonon matching rather than DOS magnitude alone.

title: Dynamical Temperley-Lieb algebras from Quiver CFTs
summary: The one-loop dilatation operator of a superconformal planar gauge theory can be written as a sum of local generators. The algebra these generators satisfy is a powerful organising principle for the spectrum. For SU(2)-like bosonic subsectors we show that this algebra can be read off directly from Feynman diagrams, which we identify as a natural graphical language for it. For N=4 super Yang-Mills this simply reproduces the Temperley-Lieb (TL) algebra of the XXX spin chain. After orbifolding and marginally deforming to N=2 superconformal quiver theories, the same recipe yields dynamical generalisations of the TL algebra. In these theories, the faces of the diagrams are coloured according to the quiver nodes, and separated by domain walls corresponding to bifundamental fields. There are two inequivalent SU(2)-like subsectors, which lead to two different TL algebras. One sector is built from the two bifundamental scalars and (in the simplest case) gives a dynamical TL algebra with a colour-dependent loop fugacity in its quadratic relation. The other sector is built from one bifundamental and one adjoint scalar, and (always) gives a novel algebra, in which the cubic TL relation becomes dynamical. In this latter case, we show that each generator of this new algebra is related to a standard XXZ TL generator by a colour-dependent twist. This twist is local and not an algebra homomorphism, and can be written as a dynamical Drinfeld twist. In both sectors, the TL structure provides a natural graphical approach to the spectral problem, as well as clarifying the structure of the irreducible representations of these chains. Finally, we give a preliminary description of the loop models associated to these algebras.

title: Black holes and 2-group symmetry from blackfolds in minimal supergravity
summary: We investigate the black hole phase diagram of five-dimensional minimal supergravity using the blackfold approach and the framework of generalized symmetries. Starting from supergravity coupled to probe sources, we derive the 2-group (non-)conservation laws, construct the equilibrium action for a two-dimensional 2-group fluid, and compute the associated global conserved charges. We then match the thermodynamics of the general non-extremal black string in the ungauged theory to that of this fluid, organizing the blackfold effective theory and its solutions in terms of symmetry invariants. In the non-extremal ungauged sector, we perturbatively construct new black rings, Saturns, di-rings, and bi-rings, including a black Saturn with seven independent parameters. Taking appropriate extremal limits, we identify several extremal branches, some previously unexplored and others anticipated, as well as BPS branches that approximate known supersymmetric families. Finally, we apply the same framework to construct extremal black rings in AdS$_5$, identifying three regular branches that are promising candidates for an exact completion.

title: Classification of Chern-Simons Couplings and Deformed Pull-Backs on D-Branes
summary:
We establish a framework for classifying higher-derivative Ramond-Ramond (RR) couplings on Dp-branes, focusing on the complete scattering amplitude of a closed-string RR state, a gauge field, and two transverse scalars. The low-energy expansion reveals infinite massless poles and local interaction terms, surpassing standard Myers and Taylor expansions. We propose a higher-class deformation of the pullback using mixed Chern-Simons transgression operators to address these complexities. Our three conjectures are as follows:
  1. For fixed field content and derivative order, effective couplings form a finite-dimensional space under stated equivalences. 2. A family of mixed RR, gauge, and scalar interactions exists at all orders, represented by a finite number of effective even forms. 3. The higher-derivative contact-term sector can be constructed from a finite set of basic tensor structures using polynomials in derivative symbols.
  We introduce a higher-class pullback operator \( P_{\infty} \) and mixed transgression operators \( \mathcal{T}_{\infty} \), emphasizing amplitude-derived pole residues and local contact terms as key physical data. This formalism distinguishes admissible tensor structures, presenting characteristic-form aspects as conjectures alongside their validity considerations.

title: Inhomogeneous Cutoff Regularization of Loops in Cosmological Correlators
summary: We revisit the use of cutoff regularization in computing loop corrections to cosmological correlators. We argue that a cutoff corresponding to a fixed physical scale must be defined with respect to the local background geometry. In the presence of superhorizon perturbations, this is naturally implemented within the separate universe picture, where different local patches are regulated at the same physical scale. Expanding this cutoff in the long-wavelength background generates a series of regulator-induced contributions to loop amplitudes, which admit a diagrammatic interpretation as long-mode insertions on the corresponding loop contractions. Our cutoff prescription preserves residual spatial dilatations and volume-preserving anisotropic rescalings. It is therefore particularly relevant for loop correlators with soft external modes. We illustrate the mechanism by computing the contributions to the one-loop scalar and tensor power spectra on superhorizon scales. In both cases, the additional corrections induced by the inhomogeneous cutoff cancel the ultraviolet boundary terms arising in the ordinary diagrams. These calculations establish, within cutoff regularization, the late-time constancy of both power spectra and clarify its physical origin. We then investigate the squeezed one-loop scalar bispectrum and show that the additional cutoff contributions are essential for satisfying the consistency relation at finite cutoff. Finally, we discuss the role of the inhomogeneous cutoff in the late-time constancy of the one-loop bispectrum.

title: Twisting Spinning Particles with Superghost Backgrounds
summary: We construct twists of spinning particles in the classical BV formalism by giving constant backgrounds to the bosonic ghosts of local worldline supersymmetry, in analogy with Costello and Li's twist of supergravity, which gives a nonzero background to the ghost of local spacetime supersymmetry. We represent the superghosts on polynomial states and gauge selected worldline R symmetries, imposing the shifted R constraints absolutely and the unshifted ones relatively. On flat targets, the N=2 particle, its N=4 extension on a complex target and an N=8 particle with two fermion flavors give the de Rham, Dolbeault and polynomial linear BCOV complexes. The last two are the linearized field content of the open and closed B-model target-space theories. Pairings and interactions require target-space input beyond the reduced worldline differentials.

title: UV Bounds on Inflationary Parity Violation
summary: A question of fundamental interest is whether parity is violated on large scales in the Universe. This possibility has been motivated by recent analyses of the four-point matter correlation function. It has also been suggested that detectable parity violation could be generated during inflation by the dynamical Chern-Simons operator, a leading effective field theory correction to general relativity. In this work, we examine this possibility in realistic UV completions, including fermionic and string-theoretic examples. We show that existing bounds on the tensor-scalar-scalar (TSS) bispectrum strongly constrain the possibility of generating a detectable parity-odd trispectrum. For tensor-to-scalar ratios near current observational limits, detectability is incompatible with, or pushes against, the regime of validity of these UV completions. A detectable signal can remain possible for a sufficiently small tensor-to-scalar ratio, but only at the cost of an extremely large enhancement of the TSS vertex. Thus, while a future search for large scale parity violation is worth pursuing, generating a detectable signal within a consistent effective theory is highly nontrivial.

title: Equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for congruence subgroups of level 2
summary: The modular properties of holomorphic Eisenstein series for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and its congruence subgroups do not carry over to their primitives. Instead, the transformation of iterated Eisenstein integrals under congruence subgroups of level $N$ introduces inhomogeneous terms comprising (among others) cyclotomic multiple zeta values of level $N$. We combine iterated Eisenstein integrals for the congruence subgroups of level $N=2$ of arbitrary iteration depth with their complex conjugates and (single-valued) level-2 cyclotomic multiple zeta values such that they define non-holomorphic modular forms. Our construction of these so-called equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for $Γ(2)$ and $Γ_0(2)$ proceeds at the level of generating series that take values in an infinite-dimensional (pro-unipotent) Lie group and closely follow Brown's analogous construction in the $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ case. The required insertions of cyclotomic multiple zeta values are controlled by zeta generators for level 2 that normalise the corresponding (pro-nilpotent) Lie algebra of the generating series and whose Lie-bracket relations we determine systematically. Upon restriction to Eisenstein series of modular weight~2, we recover single-valued multiple polylogarithms on the genus 0 modular curve $Γ(2)\backslash \mathbb{H}$.

title: Entropy Products and the Extremal Limit That Never Comes
comment: 6 pages + 1 page end matter + 24 page supplement
summary: Two regular black hole horizons need not have an entropy product fixed by the charges and couplings. In Einstein--Maxwell--scalar theory, we construct asymptotically flat branches with products above or below the squared extremal entropy. Regularity selects their horizon scalar values, and different branches can share the charges, couplings, and asymptotic scalar. Each product stays constant as mass and asymptotic scalar vary. The horizon areas stay apart and no extremal limit is reached: the temperature vanishes only where the mass diverges. We prove local existence.

title: Symmetry-resolved spectroscopy of truncation-induced perturbations in loop tensor network renormalization of the six-vertex model
summary: Tensor network renormalization at finite bond dimension $χ$ introduces truncation errors that are amplified by the renormalization-group (RG) flow. For loop tensor network renormalization (LoopTNR) on the $c=1$ critical line of the six-vertex model, with Luttinger parameter $K$, we identify these errors operator by operator from symmetry-resolved transfer-matrix spectra and conformal perturbation theory. With $O(2)$ symmetry imposed, the dominant error is the dimerization operator, which is allowed because LoopTNR breaks one-site translation. With less symmetry it is the $U(1)$ current or a charge-two vertex operator. The growth of the dimerization per RG step and a parameter-free ratio of its amplitudes agree with conformal perturbation theory to within a few percent. The parameter $K$ drifts slowly, owing to a weak marginal error and to the running induced by the dimerization. A larger $χ$ lowers the initial amplitude of the error for $0.75\le K\le 1.5$ but changes neither the operator nor its growth rate.

title: Critical droplets and metastability in long-range chains
summary: Metastable decay in first-order phase transitions proceeds through the nucleation of critical droplets. In the one-dimensional nearest-neighbor Ising chain, the cost of the two walls bounding a droplet is independent of its size. For interactions decaying as $1/r^{1+σ}$, this surface cost instead depends on the droplet size and competes with the bulk free-energy gain. The critical radius scales as $R_c\propto h^{-1/σ}$ at small $h$, where $h>0$ is the bias field. The value $σ=1$ separates two regimes: for $σ<1$, the activation barrier diverges as $h\to0^+$; at $σ=1$, it grows logarithmically; and for $σ>1$, it remains finite, as in the nearest-neighbor chain. A nonlocal $φ^4$ field theory yields critical droplets with algebraic tails and confirms the predicted radius and barrier scalings, while stochastic long-range dynamics independently reproduces the critical-radius scaling.

title: Fast extraction of universal data from temporal spectrum: Applications to Haagerup CFT and monopole scattering
comment: 10 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables; includes Supplemental Material
summary: Extracting precise universal data on conformal field theory (CFT) on the lattice traditionally requires large-scale simulations of the ground states and excitations of critical systems. Here, we propose an alternative accurate and fast algorithm, where we read off the CFT spectrum from the transfer matrix spectrum of an infinite matrix product state after a short imaginary-time evolution. We apply this method to extract the charge-resolved spectrum of a Haagerup CFT to higher levels and obtain a central charge $c = 2.137(27)$. Moreover, we show that the Maldacena--Ludwig monopole boundary can be realized as the ground state of the Fidkowski--Kitaev Hamiltonian after space-time rotation.

title: Field theory and the biquadratic spin-1 chain
summary: The antiferromagnetic biquadratic spin-1 chain is gapped, $SU(3)$ symmetric, and integrable. Standard arguments suggest that its low-energy physics is described by the $\mathbb{CP}^2$ nonlinear sigma model at $θ=π$. Using the Bethe ansatz, we show that its low-energy excitations can be interpreted as deconfined domain walls, just as in the sigma model. However, the lattice model is integrable, whereas the field theory is generally believed not to be. We propose a solution to this mystery by finding an integrable field theory with the same low-energy limit but which is not Lorentz invariant. The integrability-preserving scaling limit is obtained by adding a higher conserved charge and tuning the chain to criticality. The gap closes quadratically, so that the limit must be described by some nonrelativistic field theory rather than the relativistic sigma model. We describe the two-particle scattering matrix of this field theory.
